stem:
Diya may use only the digits $2$, $5$ and $7$. She wants 3-digit numbers that read the same forwards and backwards.

Which two claims correctly describe such palindromes?

options.text: Any arrangement of $2$, $5$ and $7$ is a palindrome.
A 3-digit palindrome must have the same hundreds digit and ones digit.
$252$ and $575$ are palindromes Diya can make from the allowed digits.
The middle digit alone decides whether the number is a palindrome.

teacher.key_rationale: A 3-digit palindrome needs matching first and last digits; 252 and 575 fit. Any arrangement is too broad; the middle digit alone is not the test.
